$comment: Declarative half of the Irr8 spectrometer pack. Edited here or in the review app's Formats tab; the behaviour is in spectrometer_irr8.py beside this file. See README.md in this folder for what each field means.
title: Irr8 spectrometer export
summary: One .Irr8.txt per recording: 1600-2050 rows of wavelength against counts, plus the acquisition header. Two of this campaign's nineteen diagnostics export this way, and one of them writes no timestamp at all.

claims.$comment: Ordered before the camera so .Irr8.txt is claimed before the camera is asked about .csv. Nothing else in a spectrometer folder is an acquisition: the .Raw8 files are two per log session, not one per shot.

namePatterns.note: German-abbreviated month and a timestamp, but a sequence number that is always 0001 and therefore carries no ordinal. The pack discards it.

No timestamp at all. The set comes from the parent folder and the ordinal from the name; the clock has to come from the filesystem, which is why time_source is recorded per record and why mounting-the-data.md insists on a copy that preserves mtimes.

$unlabelledIsShot: True: the stamped dialect sits directly in the instrument folder and declares no set, so it must stay a shot candidate and let set assignment decide from its timestamp. A camera in the same position would be an alignment series.

reader.$comment: irr8.py at the checkout root is the authority for the format and is shared with workflows/. The review app's lineouts go through shotalign/spectra.py, which reads through the same function.

nexus.$comment: ndsProfile names the reviewed NeXus Design Studio profile that governs this routing. It is checked by the combo root's `diagnostic-packs` check, which can see NDS; this repository cannot, so nothing here validates it locally.
nexus.$ndsInput: Which of this pack's files NDS is given when the review app asks it where a field belongs. 'measurement' or 'sidecar'. The .Irr8.txt itself: it carries both its header and its columns, so there is no separate sidecar to read.
nexus.$sourceAliases: Which dataset this pack writes corresponds to each field NDS names. A name not listed falls through to matching on the name itself -- `sample`, `dark`, `reference` and `photon_counts` already match their raw_data datasets exactly and need no row here. A name mapped to null is declined and never guessed.
nexus.$declined: `sequence_number` is the ordinal in the file name, which the index holds and the detector group does not. `start_time` was a null until 2026-09-25 only because nothing outside the pack's own output could be a source; it is now aliased to /entry/start_time, the shot's aligned time, as the maintainer ruled 2026-09-25. The spectrum's own time -- file_metadata/file_creation_date, from the file name in the stamped dialect (file_metadata/time_source says which), which is what NDS's profile note means -- is kept too: every detector carries it, and the spectrometer mappings link it into the subentry with a row of its own. `experiment_type`, `experiment_sub_type` and `sample_name` come from the profile's own defaults rather than from the file. Vendor and model are not in an Irr8 header at all -- only the serial is, which is why the reviewed profile carries a serial_models table.
nexus.$ambiguous: Why `absolute_irradiance` is listed when the five other spectra are not. `sample`, `dark`, `reference` and `photon_counts` each have exactly one dataset ending in their name, so the advisor's exact pass finds them and an alias would be bookkeeping. `absolute_irradiance` has two -- the measurement at raw_data/absolute_irradiance and the NXdata view of it at data/absolute_irradiance -- and two candidates make the advisor decline rather than pick, which is the right instinct and left a spectrometer's PRIMARY measurement mapped to nothing. The alias names the owner: NXdata is a view, and a mapping links the dataset the value lives in.
nexus.$signalScaleType: The scale a viewer is asked to open this format's measurement on, written as NXdata@SILX_style on the detector's `data` group and carried to the entry's plot by the builder. Opt-in: the camera pack declares nothing and nothing is written for it, which keeps one present a statement about the measurement rather than a default. 'log' here because an emission line stands four orders of magnitude above its background, so a linear axis draws a spike over an empty plot. silx knows linear, log and asinh; anything else is refused at load.
writes: raw_data/<column> — every data column the file holds, with its units
data — NXdata of irradiance against wavelength, interpretation spectrum
fabrication/serial_number — the device serial, taken from the file name
count_time — NXdetector base-class name for the header's integration time, matched by unit rather than by spelling
nexus.$unmappedSubtrees: Parts of this pack's output no mapping row is expected to claim, and why. Read by `align.py map <date> --verify`. Claiming one anyway is allowed: `averaging` does, because the Irr8 header's Averaging_Nr has no typed copy to point at instead.

unmappedSubtrees.metadata: the Irr8 header's own keys under the vendor's spelling, kept as text. count_time is the one value typed out of them; the rest have no typed copy, so a row that wants one points in here and says so.
unmappedSubtrees.data: the NXdata view of the irradiance against wavelength, made so a viewer has something to plot. Both are links to raw_data.

$registryKeys: Governed keys from DAMNIT's METADATA_KEY_REGISTRY that this pack fills. Empty: nothing in an Irr8 header is a governed quantity. governed-keys.md lists the campaign's registry mappings, all of which come from the shotsheet rather than from a diagnostic file.
notes: The set2 files carry no clock but their mtime. A copy made through FAT/exFAT or an SFTP client with a wrong timezone preference shifts every one of them by a constant, which the aligner reports as acquisitions that fit no offset and cluster into events of their own.
reference is all zeros in the December 2025 data — no calibration lamp spectrum was recorded — so absolute_irradiance is uncalibrated. The lineout endpoint reports that rather than hiding it.
